arxiv-1712-04870.title: Finite-size effects in the absorption spectra of a single-wall carbon nanotube
arxiv-1712-04870.creator: Jaime Silva, Micael J. T. Oliveira, Senentxu Lanceros-Mendez, Fernando Nogueira
arxiv-1712-04870.description: Abstract The determination of the optical spectrum of single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) is essential for the development of opto-electronic components and sensors with application in many fields. Real SWCNTs are finite, but almost all the studies performed so far use infinite SWCNTs. However, the spectra of finite and infinite systems are different.

arxiv-2101-01827.title: On the Computational Complexity of the Secure State-Reconstruction Problem 1 1 1 This work was funded in part by the Army Research Laboratory under Cooperative Agreement W911NF-17-2-0196, by the UC-NL grant LFR-18-548554, by the NSF award 1740047, and by the NSF CAREER award 1653648.
arxiv-2101-01827.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . In this paper, we discuss the computational complexity of reconstructing the state of a linear system from sensor measurements that have been corrupted by an adversary. The first result establishes that the problem is, in general, NP-hard. We then introduce the notion of eigenvalue observability and show that the state can be reconstructed in polynomial time when each eigenvalue is observable by at least 2 ​ s + 1 2s+1 sensors and at most s s sensors are corrupted by an adversary.

arxiv-2302-12686.title: Older Adults’ Task Preferences for Robot Assistance in the Home
arxiv-2302-12686.creator: Gopika Ajaykumar, Chien-Ming Huang
arxiv-2302-12686.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence technologies that can assist with at-home tasks have the potential to help older adults age in place. Robot assistance in particular has been applied towards physical and cognitive support for older adults living independently at home. Surveys, questionnaires, and group interviews have been used to understand what tasks older adults want robots to assist them with.

arxiv-2407-02322.title: Stochastic Differential Equations models for Least-Squares Stochastic Gradient Descent
arxiv-2407-02322.creator: Adrien Schertzer † and Loucas Pillaud-Vivien ⋆
arxiv-2407-02322.description: Abstract . We study the dynamics of a continuous-time model of the Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) for the least-square problem. Indeed, pursuing the work of [ 1 ] , we analyze Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) that model SGD either in the case of the training loss (finite samples) or the population one (online setting).

arxiv-2409-05729.title: Efficient estimation with incomplete data via generalised ANOVA decompositions
arxiv-2409-05729.creator: Thomas B. Berrett
arxiv-2409-05729.description: Abstract We study the semiparametric efficient estimation of a class of linear functionals in settings where a complete multivariate dataset is supplemented by additional datasets recording subsets of the variables of interest. These datasets are allowed to have a general, in particular non-monotonic, structure.

arxiv-2410-12778.title: Measuring time-resolved heat transfer fluctuations on a heated-thin foil in a turbulent channel airflow Journal: Meas. Sci. Technol.
arxiv-2410-12778.creator: A Cuéllar, E Amico, J Serpieri, G Cafiero, W J Baars, S Discetti, A Ianiro
arxiv-2410-12778.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by A Cuéllar, E Amico, J Serpieri, G Cafiero, W J Baars, S Discetti, A Ianiro. We present an experimental setup to perform time-resolved convective heat transfer measurements in a turbulent channel flow with air as the working fluid. We employ a heated thin foil coupled with high-speed infrared thermography. The measurement technique is challenged by the thermal inertia of the foil, the high frequency of turbulent fluctuations, and the measurement noise of the infrared camera.

arxiv-2503-15055.title: ELTEX: A Framework for Domain-Driven Synthetic Data Generation
arxiv-2503-15055.creator: Arina Razmyslovich, Kseniia Murasheva, Sofia Sedlova, Julien Capitaine, Eugene Dmitriev
arxiv-2503-15055.description: Abstract We introduce Efficient LLM Token Extraction (ELTEX), a framework addressing the critical challenge of LLM domain specialization by systematically extracting and integrating domain indicators throughout synthetic data generation. Unlike approaches relying on implicit knowledge transfer, ELTEX explicitly leverages domain signals to maintain specialized knowledge integrity.

arxiv-2510-00862.title: Gather-Scatter Mamba: Accelerating Propagation with Efficient State Space Model
arxiv-2510-00862.creator: Hyun-kyu Ko, Youbin Kim, Jihyeon Park, Dongheok Park, Gyeongjin Kang, Wonjun Cho, Hyung Yi, Eunbyung Park
arxiv-2510-00862.description: Abstract State Space Models (SSMs)—most notably RNNs—have historically played a central role in sequential modeling. Although attention mechanisms such as Transformers have since dominated due to their ability to model global context, their quadratic complexity and limited scalability make them less suited for long sequences. Video super-resolution (VSR) methods have traditionally relied on recurrent architectures to propagate features across frames.
